answer: An agent marketplace requires a fixed bond, locked for 90 days, for every identity allowed to bid on one job at a time. Agents offering tundra surveys, mirror inspections, or grove inventories follow the same rule. Creating more names yields no free bidding capacity: an attacker running 1,000 identities must lock 1,000 bonds. The defense makes influence scale with committed capital and costs the attacker liquidity and foregone returns for the full lock period.
